name: Rush against
caption: Turnover at their blue line. They're coming back 3-on-2 against your D, and you are the first forward back, a stride behind their trailer on the {side} side.

questions.prompt: They are coming 3-on-2. What do you do?

options.text: Skate hard and pick up their trailer on my side, staying between him and our net, so my D can play it as a 2-on-2.
options.feedback: Yes. The first forward back takes the third attacker, always. Your D handle the carrier and the far man; your job is the late option they cannot cover.

options.text: Chase the puck carrier and try to lift his stick from behind.
options.feedback: Your D already has him. A stick lift from behind is a low-percentage play and a penalty half the time, and the trailer walks in alone.

options.text: Go straight to our net front to block the shot.
options.feedback: Too deep too early. The trailer gets a free lane into the slot while you are standing at the crease. Take the man first; the net comes later.

options.text: Stay in the neutral zone so we can counter if the goalie saves it.
options.feedback: That is a 3-on-2 you chose not to help with. Backcheck first; the counter comes from winning the puck.

fb.right: The trailer. Your D have the carrier and the far winger; the late man is the one nobody else can reach.
fb.partial: That is the far winger, and your weak-side D already has him. The trailer behind the play is the uncovered man.
fb.wrong: Not the carrier; your D is on him. The first forward back always takes the third attacker, the one trailing the rush.
